title: Matrix Transformations
motto: A matrix is a machine that reshapes space. Learn what it does to every point, and you understand the whole transformation.

steps.title: Core idea
steps.body: A matrix is a machine that reshapes space. Learn what it does to every point, and you understand the whole transformation.

steps.title: Matrices reshape space
cards: PCA asks for eigenvectors of the covariance matrix. RNN stability checks whether eigenvalues have magnitude less than 1. Data augmentation applies random rotations. None of that clicks until you see matrices as spatial machines.
A rotation matrix spins points. A scaling matrix stretches them. A shearing matrix tilts them. Neural networks compose these operations layer after layer.

steps.title: Watch a unit square transform
steps.body: Every linear map is determined by where it sends the basis vectors. Drag rotation, scale, and shear — the orange square is the original unit square; blue is after the matrix hits every corner.

code.tests:
def __check(name, ok, msg=""):
    __results.append({"name": name, "pass": bool(ok), "msg": msg})

def _approx(a, b, eps=1e-4):
    return abs(a - b) < eps

try:
    import math
    R0 = rotation_2d(0)
    __check("identity", _approx(R0[0][0], 1) and _approx(R0[1][1], 1) and _approx(R0[0][1], 0))
    R90 = rotation_2d(math.pi / 2)
    p = apply_transform(R90, [1, 0])
    __check("rotate90", _approx(p[0], 0) and _approx(p[1], 1))
    p45 = apply_transform(rotation_2d(math.pi / 4), [1, 0])
    s = math.sqrt(2) / 2
    __check("rotate45", _approx(p45[0], s) and _approx(p45[1], s))
except Exception as e:
    __check("runtime", False, str(e))
